# Oplog retention sizing under burst writes
Source: https://llmsx.org/tree/oplog-retention-sizing-under-burst-writes/

# Oplog retention sizing under burst writes — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Oplog retention sizing under burst writes. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-12 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] MongoDB scopes this replica-set oplog architecture to Atlas Core and self-managed deployments; Atlas Infinite handles replication and durability in its storage layer independently of compute nodes. The replSetResizeOplog command is unsupported on MongoDB Atlas clusters; its documentation directs Atlas users to Set Minimum Oplog Window. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Oplog retention sizing under burst writes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md
- [statement] Clock drift between cluster components can cause unexpected oplog retention behavior because retention enforcement compares system wall time with entry creation wall time. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/

## How it works

- [statement] Reducing the configured size truncates oldest entries; reducing minimum retention truncates older entries when the oplog has exceeded its configured maximum size. Unreplicated truncated entries can force a secondary to resynchronize. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/
- [statement] For ApsaraDB log-backup workloads with high oplog generation, Alibaba Cloud recommends increasing oplog size or minimum retention to give the backup process time to catch up during lower traffic, and rate limiting synchronization tools through concurrency or batch size. This is product-specific guidance. (low confidence) — https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/best-practices-and-risks-for-oplog-settings
- [statement] In Ops Manager v8.0, with mms.backup.minimumOplogWindowHours set to a given value, the backup oplog-capacity check uses recent oplog usage patterns from the last 24 hours and requires at least that configured duration of oplog history over that period for all members of the replica set. A failed check prevents enabling backups under that setting; when possible, the guidance says to wait until the oplog has had sufficient time to meet the requirement. The documentation warns not to change the minimum unless smaller backups remain useful; it recommends changing the value only temporarily to permit a test backup job, then resetting the minimum to the default as soon as possible. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/v8.0/reference/troubleshooting/backup.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] MongoDB documents replSetResizeOplog against admin with size in megabytes and minRetentionHours in hours. The documented size range is 990 MB to 1 petabyte. minRetentionHours accepts fractional hours and values greater than or equal to 0; 0 selects oldest-entry truncation to maintain the configured maximum size. The documentation marks using Double() for size in mongosh as a version 5.0 change. Changing size or minimum retention affects the addressed member only; run the command on each member to change all members. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/
- [statement] IONOS Cloud's MongoDB sizing workflow budgets storage for data, indexes, journal, oplog, a 20–30% buffer and growth. It recommends an oplog window covering worst-case lag from traffic spikes, batch imports or maintenance, and verification under peak writes; its stated starting recommendation is at least 24 hours of history. The workflow's headroom guidance calls for 20–30% free storage and an oplog window at least as long as the longest maintenance window. Its example says to monitor the actual oplog window during peak write load and resize if needed. (low confidence) — https://docs.ionos.com/cloud/databases/mongodb/overview/sizing.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The oplog can grow beyond its configured size limit to avoid deleting the majority commit point. A configured oplog size is therefore not a hard disk-consumption ceiling. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md
- [statement] For Atlas deployments where oplog size is configurable, MongoDB guidance calls out intense write and update operations in a short period, advises increasing oplog size above the observed peak Oplog GB / Hour value and for anticipated intense writes, and notes that extra cluster storage may be needed to free space for resizing. The same documentation says that oplog size cannot be set on an Atlas Infinite cluster. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/replication-oplog.md
- [statement] For mongosync migrations, MongoDB documents repeated validation against retained history and actual consumer lag: use the documented db.getReplicationInfo() procedure to determine the retained oplog window in seconds on each shard and take the smallest window, then compare it with lag.overallLagSeconds from /progress. If lag approaches that minimum window, increase the window or scale the mongosync instance; replSetResizeOplog is unsupported in Atlas, whose users are directed to Set Minimum Oplog Window. The guidance says to repeat the checks because the oplog window and replication-lag rate can vary during synchronization. Source operations that roll off before mongosync applies them cause the sync to fail. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/oplog-sizing.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Minimum retention can let the oplog grow without constraint beyond its configured size to retain entries for the configured hours. High write volume combined with a long retention period can exhaust disk space. In the Percona forum, horihel specifically warns that bursty workloads can cause disk-full errors without automatic volume expansion; this is an attributed operational concern rather than a universal autoscaling requirement. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/ · keywords: Oplog retention sizing under burst writes · also: https://forums.percona.com/t/feature-proposal-oplog-management/40411

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Multi-document updates expand into individual oplog operations. Balanced insert/delete traffic and repeated in-place updates can produce substantial oplog volume without corresponding growth in stored data; database growth alone is therefore an inadequate sizing proxy. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md · keywords: Oplog retention sizing under burst writes · also: https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/best-practices-and-risks-for-oplog-settings
- [statement] With minimum retention configured, oplog entries are removed only after the oplog reaches its configured maximum size and the entries are older than the configured retention period. Retention age is evaluated against the host system clock. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md · keywords: Oplog retention sizing under burst writes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/, https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/best-practices-and-risks-for-oplog-settings
- [statement] A runtime minimum-retention change must also be recorded in startup configuration to survive restart: storage.oplogMinRetentionHours in the configuration file or --oplogMinRetentionHours on the command line. A MongoDB issue explains that size is persisted in the catalog, whereas time retention is updated in memory and reverts to startup configuration after restart. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md · keywords: Oplog retention sizing under burst writes · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-122046
- [statement] An oplog that grew beyond its configured maximum may continue to occupy that disk space after it returns to its maximum or is configured smaller. Reducing oplog size does not immediately reclaim disk space. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/
- [statement] Alibaba Cloud documents estimating oplog generation rate by dividing oplog size by oplog window. This is ApsaraDB log-backup guidance. (low confidence) — https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/best-practices-and-risks-for-oplog-settings
- [statement] MongoDB WiredTiger implementation notes describe retention enforcement at truncate-marker granularity: a marker represents a sequential range of oplog entries and may be truncated only outside the required minimum time range. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/README.md
- [statement] Percona PMM gives oplog-sizing examples that multiply oplog generation in GB/hour by 24 or 48 for a corresponding 24-hour or 48-hour window. (low confidence) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-oplog-sizing.html
- [statement] Percona PMM distinguishes Oplog Range, the time from the oldest to newest oplog entry, from Now to End, the time from the current moment to the oldest entry. Its Oplog GB/Hour metric is average primary oplog generation per hour; its documentation uses these metrics to validate sizing against a backup window. (low confidence) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html
- [statement] NVIDIA's NVSentinel v1.29.0 MongoDB Store guidance gives a HealthEvents-specific pre-load estimate: oplogSizeMB ≈ event_rate_per_sec × oplog_entry_bytes × window_seconds × extra_writes / 1_000_000. The inputs are HealthEvents inserts per second, bytes per health-event oplog insert, the required resume-token retention time, and other oplog traffic such as resume-token updates and fault-handling writes. Its preferred live recipe calculates bytesPerSec as s.size / spanSec and hoursCapacity as s.maxSize / bytesPerSec / 3600, avoiding treating an unfilled oplog as already holding the target window; it warns that resume-token heartbeats can dominate at low event rates. For this application, the same guidance keeps oplogSizeMB under about half the live PVC, budgets TTL-aged HealthEvents storage separately, and says to expand and verify the live volume before increasing oplogSizeMB. (low confidence) — https://docs.nvidia.com/nvsentinel/v1.29.0/configuration/mongo-db-store
- [statement] Alibaba Cloud documents that MongoDB 4.4 introduced storage.oplogMinRetentionHours to control the minimum oplog retention period and ensure a sufficient oplog window. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/best-practices-and-risks-for-oplog-settings
- [statement] The replSetResizeOplog command reference permits the command on mongod instances running the Wired Tiger storage engine or the in-memory storage engine. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/
- [statement] The replSetResizeOplog command takes an exclusive (W) lock on the oplog and blocks other operations on that collection until the command finishes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetResizeOplog/
